text:
maya: heads-up — customer ACME (ticket #AC-45678) saying function calls started failing after last night's model swap to open-llama-7b:v2.1. They get a schema validation error and tools aren't being invoked.

sam: can you paste the request + response they sent? any 4xx/5xx codes?

maya: here's the minimal repro (customer sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/open-llama-7b:2.1","input":"Get weather","functions":[{"name":"getWeather","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"location":{"type":"string"}},"required":["location"]}}]}'
```
response (200):
```json
{"id":"resp_1","output":"CALL_TOOL:getWhe","tool_response":null,"error":{"code":"schema_validation_failed","message":"required property 'location' is missing"}}
```

alex: thanks. canary rollout id? iirc we promoted 2.1 to canary ~0200 UTC.

maya: rollout-id rlt-2026-09-03-22, started 02:10 UTC. customer started hitting errors ~03:30 UTC.

julian: quick note from model-ops — v2.1 changed the decoding bias for tool-call tokens to reduce hallucinations, but it looks like the logits near the tool boundary are now producing truncated tokens on ~0.5-1% of calls ("getWhe" vs "getWeather"). that causes our function-dispatcher to fail schema match.

sam: i can try to repro locally. @maya can you share the full request headers (content-type, model, temp, stop tokens)?

maya: sent in DM. also customer says it worked when we reverted them to v2.0 earlier (we did a per-customer pin).

eriq: (product) how many customers affected? is it isolated to tool-heavy flows or broad?

alex: quick metrics: ~8 distinct customer tickets in last 3h referencing tool-call failures; aggregate function call failure rate spiked from 0.05% -> 0.9% during canary window. dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/dash/rollouts/rlt-2026-09-03-22 (link shared)

julian: based on that failure delta + severity (breaking API contract), recommend pausing the canary and rolling back the rollout. this is a regression vs 2.0. i can prepare a patch to force a clearer separator token and tighten decoding constraints.

maya: customer update: "we pinned back to 2.0 and they're back online, but want root cause and rollback timeline." they're asking for ETA on permanent fix.

sam: repro steps i ran locally:
```bash
python repro_toolcall.py --model redwood/open-llama-7b:2.1 --prompt 'Get weather for Boston' --seed 42
# output: CALL_TOOL:getWhe
# dispatcher logs: schema_mismatch: missing property 'location'
```

julian: thanks — matches our unit reproduction. i'll open a hotfix branch to adjust the decoding bias and add unit tests that assert full tool name tokens are emitted.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for rollout rlt-2026-09-03-22 -> target version redwood/open-llama-7b:2.0.

sam: after rollback on canary i reran the repro and tool call returned correct full name, function invoked, and schema validated.

maya: customer informed and offered one week of credits for disruption. they're OK with rollback but asked for follow-up doc on plan/fix.

eriq: i'll draft comms and timeline. engineering: can you share expected patch ETA and whether we need a security review?

julian: patch ETA ~4 hours to get tests + CI + safety checks, then hotfix deploy targeted for next maintenance window unless product approves immediate hotfix override. no additional security review needed for decoding bias change.

oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-0903 created (priority P2) — linking related tickets: AC-45678, AC-45689, AC-45690.

support-bot: marking affected tickets as escalated -> "function-calling regression (model v2.1)" and notifying customers.

maya: summary for thread: canary model v2.1 introduced decoding bias regression causing truncated tool names -> schema validation failures. rollback to v2.0 applied for impacted customers. next steps: eng-ml hotfix, add unit tests for tool-token completeness, product comms, follow-up postmortem.

alex: agree. will keep monitoring dashboard for any residual spike. :thumbsup:
